bce.body_en: Before Common Era. Enter the historical year as a positive integer (e.g. 2500 for 2500 BCE). MontuPython converts internally to astronomical year numbering for computation.
bce.body_es: Antes de la Era Comun. Ingresa el año histórico como entero positivo (p. ej. 2500 para 2500 AEC). MontuPython convierte internamente a numeración astronómica de años para el cálculo.

ce.body_en: Common Era (historically “AD”). Enter the year as a positive integer (e.g. 2026 for 2026 CE).
ce.body_es: Era Comun (históricamente "d.C."). Ingresa el año como entero positivo (p. ej. 2026 para 2026 EC).

date_proleptic.body_en:
Calendar date in the proleptic Gregorian system with historical BCE/CE years. Used to precess star coordinates to the selected epoch.

Choose era, then year, month, and day. Local time is set separately.
date_proleptic.body_es:
Fecha de calendario en el sistema gregoriano proléptico con años históricos AEC/EC. Se usa para precesar coordenadas estelares a la época seleccionada.

Elige era, luego año, mes y día. La hora local se define por separado.

day.body_en: Day of month (1–31) for the selected date. February length follows the proleptic Gregorian rules.
day.body_es: Día del mes (1-31) para la fecha seleccionada. La longitud de febrero sigue las reglas gregorianas prolépticas.

local_solar_time.body_en: Local solar civil time at the observer — hours, minutes, and seconds. With geographic longitude, MontuPython converts this instant to UTC for horizon lines, meridian view, and solar-system body positions.
local_solar_time.body_es: Hora civil solar local del observador: horas, minutos y segundos. Con la longitud geográfica, MontuPython convierte este instante a UTC para líneas de horizonte, vista meridiana y posiciones de cuerpos del sistema solar.

mag_limit_v.body_en:
Johnson V-band visual magnitude cutoff. Only objects brighter than or equal to this value are included (smaller numbers = brighter).

Reference: Sirius ≈ −1.5; naked-eye limit ≈ 6.5 under dark skies.
mag_limit_v.body_es:
Corte de magnitud visual en banda Johnson V. Solo se incluyen objetos más brillantes o iguales a este valor (números más pequeños = más brillantes).

Referencia: Sirio ≈ -1.5; límite a simple vista ≈ 6.5 en cielos oscuros.

observer_location.body_en:
Geographic observing site shared by all sky modules. Set latitude, longitude, and altitude in the 🧭 Observer Location module; the label here shows the active site.

Latitude and longitude define the local horizon, sidereal time, and azimuth/elevation; altitude [m] is converted to kilometres for montu.Observer.
observer_location.body_es:
Sitio geográfico de observación compartido por todos los módulos del cielo. Define latitud, longitud y altitud en el módulo 🧭 Ubicación del observador; la etiqueta aqui muestra el sitio activo.

La latitud y la longitud definen el horizonte local, el tiempo sideral y el azimut/elevación; la altitud [m] se convierte a kilómetros para montu.Observer.

year.body_en:
Calendar year as a positive integer together with the selected BCE or CE era.

Example: 2500 with BCE → year 2500 BCE.
year.body_es:
Año de calendario como entero positivo junto con la era seleccionada AEC o EC.

Ejemplo: 2500 con AEC -> año 2500 AEC.

map.body_en:
Mercator sky map at the midpoint epoch of the search range (RA vs declination).

Elements:

  • White circles — bright stars in their precessed positions
  • Gold stars ★ — aligned stars
  • Gold dashed line — target declination
  • Gold shaded band — declination tolerance
  • Blue dotted line — circumpolar limit: stars beyond this declination never set at the observer latitude (northern sites: dec ≥ limit; southern sites: dec ≤ limit).

Hover over any star for name, coordinates, magnitude, and alignment details.
map.body_es: Mapa de cielo tipo Mercator en la época media del rango de búsqueda (AR vs declinación). Incluye estrellas, banda de tolerancia y línea de declinación objetivo.

table.body_en:
Lists every star whose precessed declination falls within ±tolerance of the target declination at any sampled epoch.

Columns:

  • Star — proper name (e.g. Thuban) or catalogue name
  • V mag — Johnson V visual magnitude
  • RA at best epoch — right ascension at the year of closest approach, in h m s
  • Dec at best epoch — declination at the year of closest approach
  • Δ Dec — absolute difference between star declination and target
  • Best year — the sampled epoch at which the star was closest to the target declination
table.body_es: Lista cada estrella cuya declinación precesada cae dentro de ±tolerancia respecto a la declinación objetivo en algún época muestreada.

azimuth.body_en:
Horizontal compass bearing of the alignment direction, measured clockwise from true North.

  • 0° = North (e.g. the northern shafts of the Great Pyramid)
  • 90° = East (objects rise due East only on the celestial equator)
  • 180° = South (southern shafts of the Great Pyramid point here)
  • 270° = West

The azimuth, together with the elevation and the observer latitude, uniquely determines the target declination shown below the inputs.
azimuth.body_es: Rumbo horizontal de la dirección de alineamiento, medido en sentido horario desde el norte verdadero.

dec_tolerance.body_en:
Half-width of the declination band around the target [degrees]. A star is reported as aligned when its epoch-of-date declination falls within target ± tolerance.

Rule of thumb:

  • 0.5° ≈ 30 arcminutes — tight constraint, exact alignments only
  • 1° — default in famous-alignment presets
  • 2°+ — wider margin for shaft width and measurement uncertainty
dec_tolerance.body_es: Semiancho de la banda de declinación alrededor del objetivo [grados].

elevation.body_en:
Angle above the horizon [degrees] of the alignment direction.

Examples from the Great Pyramid of Khufu:

  • King's Chamber northern shaft — elevation ≈ 31.7°
  • King's Chamber southern shaft — elevation ≈ 44.5°
  • Queen's Chamber northern shaft — elevation ≈ 39.6°
  • Queen's Chamber southern shaft — elevation ≈ 39.6°

Horizontal (0°) points to the horizon; vertical (90°) points to the zenith.
elevation.body_es: Angulo sobre el horizonte [grados] de la dirección de alineamiento.

famous_alignments.body_en:
Load a documented archaeological sky alignment from assets/alignments.json. Selecting a preset fills the observer site, azimuth, elevation, date range, limiting magnitude, and declination tolerance.

Presets include:

  • Khufu north/south shafts — Great Pyramid of Giza (Old Kingdom)
  • Djoser serdab — Step Pyramid at Saqqara (3rd Dynasty)
  • Senenmut TT353 — tomb-temple entrance at Deir el-Bahari (1472–1457 BCE)
famous_alignments.body_es: Carga un alineamiento arqueoastronómico documentado desde assets/alignments.json. El preset rellena sitio, azimut, elevación, rango temporal, magnitud límite y tolerancia en declinación.

mag_limit.body_en:
Only stars with a Johnson V-band visual magnitude brighter than or equal to this value are included.

Examples of reference magnitudes:

  • Sirius (brightest star) — V = −1.46
  • Thuban (α Draconis, Great Pyramid alignment) — V ≈ 3.65
  • Naked-eye limit under dark skies — V ≈ 6.5

Lower values (e.g. 2) restrict the search to the very brightest stars; higher values (e.g. 6) include fainter ones but slow computation.
mag_limit.body_es: Solo se incluyen estrellas con magnitud visual Johnson V más brillante o igual a este valor.

year_end.body_en:
End of the search interval. Enter a positive year and select BCE or CE.

Default: 2420 BCE — about 140 years after the nominal construction date. Widening this range increases the chance of catching stars whose alignment window overlaps the range.
year_end.body_es: Fin del intervalo de búsqueda. Ingresa un año positivo y selecciona AEC o EC.

year_start.body_en:
Start of the search interval. Enter a positive year and select BCE or CE.

The module will sample the stellar catalogue at several epochs between the start and end years, precessing each star's coordinates to the epoch-of-date system.

Default: 2620 BCE — slightly before the accepted construction date of the Great Pyramid (~2 560 BCE).
year_start.body_es: Inicio del intervalo de búsqueda. Ingresa un año positivo y selecciona AEC o EC.

historical_dates.body_en:
Preset historical dates from the past whose instant is known in more than one calendar system — typically as a Julian/Gregorian date and as an Egyptian civil (caniucular) date, and sometimes with a lunar or documentary context. Select an entry to load it into all input forms and the results table.

Most entries come from the astronomy of ancient Egypt as discussed by the Egyptologist José Lull in La astronomía en el antiguo Egipto (Astronomy in Ancient Egypt, Universitat de València). Page references below are to that book unless noted otherwise.

Presets and sources

  • BCE 2782-07-20 — First apokatastasis (caniucular datum hrw 0-I-Akhet-1); Lull, calendar chapter
  • BCE 1322-07-20 — Second apokatastasis; Lull
  • CE 139-07-20 — Third apokatastasis (Censorinus); Lull, p. 95
  • BCE 559-10-19 — Papyrus Louvre 7848 (civil + lunar dates); Lull, p. 94
  • BCE 238-03-07 — Canopus decree; Lull, p. 76
  • BCE 237-08-23 / BCE 212-08-17 — Edfu temple inscriptions (25-year lunar cycle); Lull, p. 92
  • CE 384-07-23 — Theon of Alexandria, heliacal rise of Sirius; Lull, p. 98
  • BCE 688-06-11 — Papyrus Louvre E3228d (Taharqa, year 3); Lull, p. 105
  • BCE 46-01-01 — Julian calendar reform (Sosigenes); Suetonius, Divus Julius
historical_dates.body_es:
Fechas históricas predefinidas con correspondencias entre calendarios (juliano/gregoriano, caniucular, y en algunos casos contexto lunar o documental).

La mayoria de entradas provienen de la astronomía del antiguo Egipto descrita por José Lull en La astronomía en el antiguo Egipto.

caniucular.body_en: Enter a date in the Egyptian civil calendar: Horus year, month (I–IV within the season), season name, and day (1–30). Each season has four months of 30 days.
caniucular.body_es: Ingresa una fecha del calendario civil egipcio: año de Horus, mes (I-IV), estacion y día (1-30).

caniucular_day.body_en:
Day within the current month and season. Regular seasons use days 1–30; the intercalary season Mesut uses days 1–5 only.

Format

  • Integer day in hrw HYEAR-MONTH-SEASON-DAY
  • Range 1–30 (Akhet, Peret, Shemu) or 1–5 (Mesut)

Examples

  • 1 — first day of the month/season block
  • 30 — last day of a regular month (e.g. IV-Shemu-30)
  • 3 on Mesut — third epagomenal day before the new year
caniucular_day.body_es: Día dentro del mes y estacion actuales. En estaciones regulares: 1-30. En Mesut: 1-5.

caniucular_month.body_en:
Month within the current season in the Egyptian civil calendar. Each season has four months, numbered with Roman numerals I–IV (not the 12 Gregorian months).

Format

  • One of: I, II, III, IV
  • Third field in hrw HYEAR-MONTH-SEASON-DAY

Examples

  • I — first month of the season (days 1–30)
  • IV — fourth and last month of the season
  • hrw 0-I-Akhet-1 — month I of season Akhet at the datum
caniucular_month.body_es: Mes dentro de la estacion actual en calendario civil egipcio. Cada estacion tiene cuatro meses: I-IV.

caniucular_offset.body_en:
Use − and + to move one civil day backward or forward from the current caniucular date. All input forms and the results table update immediately.

Examples

  • IV-Shemu-30 then + → I-Mesut-1
  • I-Mesut-5 then + → I-Akhet-1 of the next Horus year
  • − reverses the same transitions
caniucular_offset.body_es: Usa - y + para mover un día civil hacia atras o adelante desde la fecha caniucular actual.

caniucular_season.body_en:
Season name in the Egyptian civil calendar. The year is divided into three seasons of 120 days (Akhet, Peret, Shemu), plus an optional intercalary period (Mesut).

Format

  • One of: Akhet, Peret, Shemu, Mesut
  • Akhet — inundation; Peret — emergence; Shemu — harvest; Mesut — epagomenal days (5 days after Shemu IV-30)

Examples

  • Akhet — first season; contains hrw 0-I-Akhet-1
  • Shemu — e.g. hrw 4809-III-Shemu-25 for a modern March date
  • Mesut — epagomenal days 1–5; e.g. day after IV-Shemu-30 is I-Mesut-1

date_grid_weekdays.body_en:
The month grid is a date picker in Gregorian style. Its weekday columns follow the proleptic Gregorian layout because Qt’s calendar widget and the desktop UI use that convention internally — not necessarily the weekday of your chosen Mixed or BCE calendar rules.

To know the true day of the week for the converted instant, read the Weekday row in the conversion results (from MontuPython).

Example: 1582-10-04 in Mixed (still Julian) was a Thursday — output shows Thursday (5) — but the grid for October 1582 places the 4th under Monday, because the grid uses the proleptic Gregorian alignment for that civil date.
date_grid_weekdays.body_es:
La cuadrícula de mes es un selector de fechas en estilo gregoriano. Sus columnas de día de semana siguen la convención gregoriana proleptica usada por Qt.

Para conocer el día de semana real del instante convertido, consulta la fila Día de la semana en resultados.
date_grid_weekdays.title_es: Fecha (estilo gregoriano, días de semana prolépticos)

historical_dates.body_en: Select a preset date from Egyptology and astronomy literature. See also the full help under Historical dates (input mode) or Historical Date above the preset list for sources, including José Lull’s La astronomía en el antiguo Egipto.
historical_dates.body_es: Selecciona una fecha predefinida de literatura de egiptología y astronomía.

horus_year.body_en:
Year in the Egyptian civil calendar counted from the Horus (caniucular) epoch. Year 0 is anchored at the first apokatastasis (hrw 0-I-Akhet-1 = BCE 2782-07-20).

Format

  • Integer (may be negative for years before the epoch in some displays)
  • Appears as the first number in hrw HYEAR-MONTH-SEASON-DAY

Examples

  • 0 — epoch year (datum)
  • 1 — one civil year after the datum
  • 4809 — modern date in Horus years (e.g. 2026 CE)
horus_year.body_es: Año del calendario civil egipcio contado desde la época caniucular (hrw 0-I-Akhet-1).

julian_day.body_en: Enter a Julian Day Number (UTC scale), optionally with a fractional part for the time of day. Example: 2461231.5 is noon on that Julian day.
julian_day.body_es: Ingresa un Numero de Día Juliano (escala UTC), opcionalmente con parte fraccionaria para la hora.

julian_day_utc.body_en:
Julian Day Number on the UTC scale (Time.jed). Enter days and an optional fractional part for the time of day. This is the primary numeric input when converting from JD to all calendar formats.

Format

  • Decimal: integer.fraction
  • Fraction .0 = noon at the start of that JD; .5 = midnight in common conventions

Examples

  • 2451545.0 — J2000.0 epoch
  • 2461231.5 — noon on that Julian day
  • 625307.5 — default sample value in this form
julian_day_utc.body_es: Numero de Día Juliano en escala UTC (Time.jed). Ingresa días y fraccion opcional para la hora.

julian_gregorian.body_en: Enter a date in the familiar Gregorian-style calendar. Choose BCE or CE, Mixed or Proleptic calendar type, then pick the date and time. Results update automatically as you change any field.
julian_gregorian.body_es: Ingresa una fecha en calendario tipo gregoriano. Elige AEC o EC, tipo mixto o proléptico, y luego fecha y hora.

mixed.body_en: Use the historically correct calendar rules: Julian calendar before the 1582 reform, Gregorian calendar afterward. Recommended for real historical dates.
mixed.body_es: Usa reglas históricas: calendario juliano antes de 1582 y gregoriano despues.

proleptic.body_en: Extend Gregorian calendar rules backward for the entire timeline. No Julian–Gregorian switch — useful for uniform astronomical or mathematical dating.
proleptic.body_es: Extiende las reglas gregorianas hacia atras en toda la línea temporal.

caniucular.body_en:
Date in the Egyptian civil (caniucular) calendar (Time.readable.datecan): Horus year, month, season, and day. The year begins with the heliacal rise of Sirius (Sothis); the epoch is hrw 0-I-Akhet-1 = BCE 2782-07-20.

Format

  • hrw HYEAR-MONTH-SEASON-DAY
  • HYEAR — year of Horus (integer, may be negative in display)
  • MONTH — Roman numeral I–IV within the season
  • SEASON — Akhet, Peret, Shemu, or Mesut (intercalary)
  • DAY — 1–30

Examples

  • hrw 0-I-Akhet-1 — caniucular epoch (datum)
  • hrw 1-I-Akhet-2 — day after the datum in Horus year 1
  • hrw 4809-III-Shemu-25 — 7 March 2026 CE in civil form
caniucular.body_es: Fecha en el calendario civil egipcio (caniucular) (Time.readable.datecan): año de Horus, mes, estacion y día.

delta_t.body_en:
Difference TT − UTC in seconds (Time.deltat). Accounts for irregular Earth rotation (tidal braking and leap seconds). Required to convert between civil UTC and uniform TT.

Format

  • Decimal seconds (positive in the modern era: TT runs ahead of UTC)
  • Tabulated internally by MontuPython for historical dates

Examples

  • 67.184 — approximate value near 2020 CE
  • 67692.000 — much larger for ancient dates (e.g. BCE 2782), where extrapolation uncertainty is high
delta_t.body_es: Diferencia TT - UTC en segundos (Time.deltat). Considera la rotacion irregular de la Tierra y es necesaria para convertir entre UTC civil y TT uniforme.

et.body_en:
Ephemeris seconds on the UTC scale, measured from J2000.0. Corresponds to Time.et. In MontuPython: et = tt − deltat.

Format

  • Decimal seconds from J2000.0 (UTC)
  • Differs from TT by Delta-T (Earth rotation effects)

Examples

  • 0.0 — J2000.0 (UTC ephemeris time origin)
  • For any date, typically a few tens of seconds less than the TT value at the same instant (see Delta-T)
et.body_es: Segundos de efemérides en escala UTC medidos desde J2000.0. Corresponde a Time.et. En MontuPython: et = tt - deltat.

jd_utc.body_en:
Julian Day Number on the UTC scale (Time.jed). Counts days and fraction from the Julian epoch (1 January 4713 BCE, 12:00 TT). A pure number — not a calendar string.

Format

  • Decimal number: integer.fraction
  • Fraction 0.0 = noon at the beginning of that JD; 0.5 = midnight; add 0.5 to move from noon-based JD to midnight-based conventions if needed
  • Typically shown with 6 decimal places in this table

Examples

  • 2451545.0 — J2000.0 (2000-01-01 12:00 TT ≈ standard epoch)
  • 2461231.5 — noon on a modern Julian day
  • 705863.500000 — caniucular datum region (BCE 2782-07-20)
jd_utc.body_es: Numero de Día Juliano en escala UTC (Time.jed). Cuenta días y fraccion desde la época juliana. Es un numero, no una cadena de calendario.

mixed.body_en:
Calendar date in the mixed convention (Time.readable.datemix): Julian calendar before 15 October 1582, Gregorian from the reform onward. This is the usual choice for real historical dates.

Format

  • YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS for CE dates
  • -YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS for BCE dates (minus prefix on astronomical year)
  • Month lengths follow the active calendar (Julian or Gregorian) for that date

Examples

  • 2026-03-07 14:30:30 — modern date (Gregorian rules)
  • 1582-10-04 00:00:00 — last Julian day before the 1582 reform (in affected countries)
  • -2780-07-20 00:00:00 — ancient date under Julian rules (near the caniucular datum)
mixed.body_es: Fecha de calendario en convención mixta (Time.readable.datemix): juliano antes del 15 de octubre de 1582 y gregoriano desde la reforma en adelante.

proleptic.body_en:
Proleptic Gregorian date in the astronomical year convention (Time.readable.datepro): year 0 = 1 BCE, year −1 = 2 BCE, etc. Useful for continuous calculations without a gap at year 1.

Format

  • YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffff for CE dates
  • -YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffff for BCE dates (leading minus on the astronomical year)
  • ISO-like ordering: year, month, day, then 24-hour time

Examples

  • 2026-03-07 14:30:00.0000 — 7 March 2026 CE
  • -2780-06-27 00:00:00.0000 — astronomical year −2780 (= 2781 BCE)
  • -0001-01-01 00:00:00.0000 — 1 BCE (astronomical year 0 is 1 BCE in historical terms)
proleptic.body_es: Fecha gregoriana proleptica en convención de año astronómico (Time.readable.datepro): año 0 = 1 AEC, año -1 = 2 AEC, etc.

spice.body_en:
Human-readable proleptic Gregorian date in SPICE / NASA style (Time.readable.datespice). The proleptic Gregorian calendar extends Gregorian rules backward without the historical Julian–Gregorian transition.

Format

  • CE: YYYY A.D. MM-DD HH:MM:SS.μμ
  • BCE: YYYY B.C. MM-DD HH:MM:SS.μμ (year shown as historical BCE count)
  • Month and day are MM-DD (not ISO order)
  • Fractional seconds use two or four digits after the decimal point

Examples

  • 2026 A.D. 03-07 14:30:00.0000 — 7 March 2026, 14:30 CE
  • 2781 B.C. 06-27 00:00:00.00 — caniucular datum region (BCE 2782-07-20 input)
  • 0100 B.C. 03-15 06:00:00.00 — 15 March 100 BCE
spice.body_es: Fecha gregoriana proleptica legible en estilo SPICE / NASA (Time.readable.datespice). El calendario gregoriano proléptico extiende las reglas gregorianas hacia atras sin la transición histórica juliano-gregoriana.

tt.body_en:
Ephemeris seconds on the TT (Terrestrial Time) scale, measured from J2000.0 (2000-01-01 12:00 TT). Corresponds to Time.tt. Not a Julian Day — it is a uniform atomic-time-style count used by SPICE and many ephemerides.

Format

  • Decimal seconds (may be negative for dates before J2000)
  • Uniform scale — no leap seconds

Examples

  • 0.0 — J2000.0 epoch
  • 86400.0 — one TT day after J2000.0
  • Large negative values for ancient dates (e.g. near BCE 2782)
tt.body_es: Segundos de efemérides en escala TT (Tiempo Terrestre) medidos desde J2000.0. Corresponde a Time.tt.

weekday.body_en:
Day of the week for the converted instant (Time.readable.weekday and weekday_name).

Format: English name + number in parentheses. MontuPython convention: 1 = Sunday … 7 = Saturday.

Examples: Friday (6), Wednesday (4).
weekday.body_es:
Día de la semana para el instante convertido (Time.readable.weekday y weekday_name).

Formato: nombre en inglés + numero entre parentesis. Convencion de MontuPython: 1 = domingo ... 7 = sabado.

body_en.title: Celestial body
body_en.body: Body whose first visible morning appearance is sought. A heliacal rise is reported when the body is visible under the selected model after having been invisible on the preceding morning.

body_es.title: Cuerpo celeste
body_es.body: Cuerpo cuya primera aparicion matutina visible se busca. Se reporta un orto helíaco cuando el cuerpo es visible segun el modelo seleccionado tras haber sido invisible la manana anterior.

body_type.body_en: Select a star from the named bright-star catalogue or one of the visible classical planets. The calculation uses the catalogue V magnitude for stars and the ephemeris magnitude at each evaluated instant for planets.
body_type.body_es: Selecciona una estrella del catálogo de estrellas brillantes con nombre o uno de los planetas clásicos visibles.

calendar.body_en:
Select the calendar interpretation of the initial date.

  • Mixed — Julian calendar before 15 October 1582 and Gregorian thereafter. This is the default and is recommended for historical dates, including the 139 BCE caniucular context.
  • Proleptic — Gregorian rules extended uniformly into the past. Use it for astronomical or mathematical date ranges that require a single calendar system.
calendar.body_es:
Selecciona la interpretacion de calendario de la fecha inicial.

  • Mixto: juliano antes de 1582 y gregoriano despues.
  • Proleptico: reglas gregorianas extendidas uniformemente al pasado.

initial_date.body_en: First civil date of the search interval. Choose BCE or CE, then year, month, and day. The default is 2782 BCE, 1 June — near the first apokatastasis in the historical presets.
initial_date.body_es: Primera fecha civil del intervalo de búsqueda. Elige AEC o EC, luego año, mes y día.

k.body_en: Visual atmospheric extinction coefficient in magnitudes per air mass. It dims objects nearer the horizon. Default: 0.25 mag/air mass.
k.body_es: Coeficiente de extincion atmosferica visual en magnitudes por masa de aire.

limiting_mag_zenith.body_en: Faintest visible visual magnitude at the zenith for the Schaefer models. Smaller magnitudes are brighter; a larger value assumes a darker, more transparent sky. Default: 6.0.
limiting_mag_zenith.body_es: Magnitud visual límite en el cenit para los modelos de Schaefer.

model.body_en:
Observational model used to decide whether the body is visible at morning twilight.

  • Schaefer 1985 — twilight sky brightness, atmospheric extinction, and a point-source threshold; reconstructed from the published Sky & Telescope BASIC listing.
  • Schaefer 1987 — evaluates visibility at a fixed Sun depression using secant airmass and a zenith limiting magnitude.
  • Belokrylov et al. 2011 — atmospheric absorption, bright-star regressions, and a Sun–star separation correction.
  • Ptolemy (Arcus Visionis) — computes solar depression at the body's horizon crossing and compares it against a critical Arcus Visionis threshold.

The bibliographic source for the active model appears below the results.
model.body_es: Modelo observaciónal usado para decidir si el cuerpo es visible en el crepusculo matutino.

reference_extinction.body_en: Reference extinction in equation (6) of the Belokrylov et al. (2011) model, in magnitudes per air mass. Default: 0.25.
reference_extinction.body_es: Extincion de referencia en la ecuacion (6) del modelo de Belokrylov et al. (2011).

arcus_visionis_crit.body_en: Critical Arcus Visionis threshold [degrees] for the Ptolemy model. The body is considered visible only when the computed Sun depression at horizon crossing is equal to or greater than this value.
arcus_visionis_crit.body_es: Umbral critico del Arcus Visionis [grados] para el modelo de Ptolomeo. El cuerpo se considera visible cuando la depresion solar calculada en el cruce del horizonte es mayor o igual a este valor.

ptolemy_refraction_deg.body_en: Horizon refraction entered in arcminutes for the Ptolemy model when solving body horizon crossing. The app converts this value internally to degrees before calling MontuPython. Default is 0 arcmin, since in this historical-use context the body is considered already emerged above the horizon and the correction is negligible.
ptolemy_refraction_deg.body_es: Refraccion de horizonte ingresada en minutos de arco para el modelo de Ptolomeo al resolver el cruce de horizonte del cuerpo. La app convierte este valor internamente a grados antes de llamar a MontuPython. El valor por defecto es 0 min de arco, porque en este contexto historico se considera que el cuerpo ya habia emergido sobre el horizonte y la correccion es despreciable.

step_minutes.body_en: Time step [minutes] used while scanning morning twilight in the Schaefer 1985 and Belokrylov 2011 models. Smaller steps locate the first visible instant more precisely but increase calculation time. Default: 2 minutes.
step_minutes.body_es: Paso temporal [minutos] usado al escanear el crepusculo matutino en Schaefer 1985 y Belokrylov 2011.

sun_depression.body_en: Solar altitude below the horizon [degrees] at which the Schaefer 1987 criterion is evaluated. It must be negative. Default: −11°.
sun_depression.body_es: Altitud solar bajo el horizonte [grados] para evaluar el criterio de Schaefer 1987.

twilight_sunbelow.body_en: Solar depression [degrees] that marks the start of the morning-twilight scan for Schaefer 1985 and Belokrylov 2011. Default: −18°, astronomical dawn.
twilight_sunbelow.body_es: Depresion solar [grados] que marca el inicio del escaneo de crepusculo matutino.

year_range.body_en:
Length of the search interval in years, starting at the initial date. The calculator evaluates the selected visibility model one morning at a time; longer intervals take proportionally longer.

Warning: scan-based models and long intervals can take time to complete.
year_range.body_es: Longitud del intervalo de búsqueda en años, desde la fecha inicial.

peret_sopedet.body_en:
Peret Sopedet (emergence of Sopedet) is the Egyptian civil-year marker tied to the heliacal rise of Sirius — Sothis in Greek, Sopedet (spdt) in Egyptian. Its first morning visibility after a period of invisibility opened the season Akhet and the civil New Year (hrw 0-I-Akhet-1).

The illustration below depicts that heliacal rising of Sirius beside the pyramids on the Giza plateau.

Image credit

This illustration was generated with Nano Banana, edited in Preview, and is based on the realistic simulation created with Stellarium and GIMP by Bob Moler and published on Bob Moler's Ephemeris Blog: Sirius: an important star in history (7 February 2017).
peret_sopedet.body_es: Peret Sopedet (emergencia de Sopedet) es el marcador del año civil egipcio ligado al orto helíaco de Sirio.

table.body_en:
Each row is a morning on which the selected body became visible under the selected model after being invisible on the preceding morning.

  • # — event sequence number.
  • Date mixed, Date proleptic, and Date caniucular — the same instant in Time.readable.datemix, datepro, and datecan.
  • Time from latest — days since the prior heliacal rise; for event 1, days since the initial date.
  • Local time — local solar time at the evaluated visible instant.
  • Altitude and azimuth — apparent horizontal coordinates of the body and Sun in degrees. Azimuth is measured clockwise from North.
table.body_es: Cada fila corresponde a una manana en la que el cuerpo seleccionado se vuelve visible segun el modelo elegido, tras haber sido invisible la manana anterior.

altitude.body_en: Elevation above mean sea level in metres. Converted internally to kilometres for montu.Observer. When you click the map, MontuPython queries the free Open-Elevation service.
altitude.body_es: Elevacion sobre el nivel medio del mar en metros. Se convierte internamente a kilómetros para montu.Observer.

decimal.body_en:
Enter coordinates as decimal degrees (DD.dddddd°). Positive latitude = north, negative = south. Positive longitude = east, negative = west.

Example: Luxor → lat 25.6967, lon 32.6422.
decimal.body_es: Ingresa coordenadas en grados decimales. Latitud positiva = norte, negativa = sur. Longitud positiva = este, negativa = oeste.

latitude.body_en: Geodetic latitude of the observing site [degrees]. North positive, south negative. Range: −90° … +90°.
latitude.body_es: Latitud geodesica del sitio de observación [grados]. Norte positivo, sur negativo.

longitude.body_en: Geodetic longitude of the observing site [degrees]. East positive, west negative. Range: −180° … +180°.
longitude.body_es: Longitud geodesica del sitio de observación [grados]. Este positivo, oeste negativo.

map_labels.body_en:
Choose how place names appear on the map tiles.

  • Local names — standard OpenStreetMap tiles (e.g. Arabic in Egypt).
  • English names — Wikimedia internationalized tiles that prefer name:en where available.

Switching reloads the map. Your choice is remembered for future sessions.
map_labels.body_es: Elige como se muestran los nombres de lugares en los mosaicos del mapa: nombres locales o nombres en inglés.

predefined.body_en:
Search or select an ancient-world location from assets/locations.json. Choosing a site fills latitude, longitude, and altitude automatically.

Default at startup: Thebes (Luxor), capital of ancient Upper Egypt.
predefined.body_es: Busca o selecciona un lugar del mundo antiguo en assets/locations.json. Al elegirlo, se rellenan latitud, longitud y altitud automáticamente.

sexagesimal.body_en:
Enter coordinates as degrees, arcminutes, and arcseconds with a hemisphere letter (N/S for latitude, E/W for longitude). Altitude remains in metres.

Example: 25°41'48.1"N, 32°38'32.0"E.
sexagesimal.body_es: Ingresa coordenadas en grados, minutos y segundos con hemisferio (N/S para latitud, E/W para longitud).

add_body.body_en:
Choose a Sun, Moon, planet, or named star from the dropdown and click ＋ Add. Each body appears as a row on the disk with its own effective horizon altitude.

The star list respects the V magnitude filter below. Duplicate bodies are not allowed. At least one body must remain on the disk.

From the reference year, MontuPython sweeps max(2 years, orbital period) per body and finds the northernmost and southernmost rise (△) and set (▽) azimuths.
add_body.body_es: Elige Sol, Luna, planeta o estrella nombrada en el desplegable y haz clic en + Agregar. Cada cuerpo aparece como una fila en el disco con su propia altitud efectiva de horizonte.

reference_year.body_en:
Start year of the search window. The sweep length is max(2 years, orbital period) for each body (the Sun uses 2 years). Select BCE or CE and enter the historical year.

Extreme rise/set azimuths are sampled over this interval at the observer site.
reference_year.body_es: Año de inicio de la ventana de búsqueda. La longitud del barrido es max(2 años, período orbital) para cada cuerpo.

star_mag_filter.body_en:
Filters which named stars appear in the add-body dropdown. Only stars brighter than or equal to this Johnson V magnitude are listed.

Does not affect planets or the Sun/Moon. Lower values show fewer, brighter stars.
star_mag_filter.body_es: Filtra que estrellas nombradas aparecen en el desplegable de agregar cuerpo. Solo se listan estrellas más brillantes o iguales a esa magnitud V.

chart.body_en:
The initial date in Parameters uses the proleptic Gregorian calendar with historical BCE/CE years — e.g. entering 1500 BCE means the year 1500 before the Common Era.

The chart X-axis and the hover tooltip datestr show proleptic Gregorian dates in astronomical year numbering (e.g. May 12, -1499 = 12 May 1500 BCE; there is no year 0, so 1 BCE = year 0).

The plot title uses the human-readable proleptic form (e.g. 1500 B.C. 01-01).

Hover over any point on the curve to read datestr (proleptic Gregorian, astronomical), Julian day (JD), and the selected property value. Use the rangeslider below the plot to zoom the time axis.
chart.body_es: Pasa el cursor sobre la curva para leer fecha, día juliano y valor de la propiedad seleccionada. Usa el rango inferior para acercar el eje de tiempo.

initial_date.body_en:
Start of the ephemeris interval in the proleptic Gregorian calendar using historical BCE/CE years.

Choose BCE or CE, then year, month, and day. Example: 1500 BCE, 1 January is year 1500 before the Common Era — internally converted to astronomical year −1499 for computation.

The chart axis shows astronomical proleptic dates (datepro); the title uses the human-readable SPICE-style form (1500 B.C. 01-01).
initial_date.body_es: Inicio del intervalo de efemérides en calendario gregoriano proléptico usando años históricos AEC/EC.

num_points.body_en:
How many evenly spaced time steps to compute along the interval. More points give a smoother curve but take longer to calculate.

Minimum: 2. Default in Montu App: 120.
num_points.body_es: Cantidad de pasos de tiempo equiespaciados a calcular en el intervalo.

planets.body_en:
Select one or more classical wanderers to plot. In antiquity the word planet (Greek planētēs, “wanderer”) included the Sun and Moon along with Mercury, Venus, Mars, Júpiter, and Saturn — seven bodies that move against the fixed stars.

Available here: Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Júpiter, Saturn. Each selection appears as a separate coloured line. Uranus, Neptune, and Earth are excluded.
planets.body_es: Selecciona uno o más astros errantes clásicos para graficar: Sol, Luna, Mercurio, Venus, Marte, Júpiter y Saturno.

property.body_en: Ephemeris quantity plotted on the Y-axis. The dropdown shows friendly quantity names; the full catalogue is loaded from assets/planet_properties.json.
property.body_es: Magnitud de efemérides a graficar en el eje Y.

time_span.body_en:
Duration of the sample interval in years (not days or months). The module builds an evenly spaced grid from the initial date through this span.

Example: initial date -1500-01-01 and span 10 covers roughly 1500 BCE to 1490 BCE.
time_span.body_es: Duracion del intervalo de muestreo en años (no días ni meses).

gregorian_proleptic.body_en:
Human-readable proleptic Gregorian date in SPICE / NASA style (Time.readable.datespice).

Format: YYYY A.D. MM-DD HH:MM:SS.μμ (CE) or YYYY B.C. MM-DD HH:MM:SS.μμ (BCE).
gregorian_proleptic.body_es: Fecha gregoriana proleptica legible en estilo SPICE / NASA.

mixed.body_en:
Date in the mixed calendar convention (Time.readable.datemix): Julian before 1582-10-15, Gregorian afterward.

Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (CE) or -YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (BCE, astronomical year).
mixed.body_es: Fecha en convención mixta: juliano antes de 1582-10-15, gregoriano despues.

quarter_delta_t.body_en:
Elapsed time in days since the previous lunar quarter phase (new, first, full, or last).

For the first quarter listed in the year, counted from the last quarter before 1 January.

Typical values: ~7 days (new → first), ~7 days (first → full), ~7 days (full → last), ~7 days (last → new).
quarter_delta_t.body_es: Tiempo transcurrido en días desde la fase lunar de cuarto anterior.

season_delta_t.body_en:
Elapsed time in days since the previous astronomical season event.

  • For the Northward equinox, counted from the previous Southern solstice.
  • For subsequent seasons, counted from the immediately preceding season in the same year.

Based on the difference of Julian Day numbers returned by MontuPython.
season_delta_t.body_es: Tiempo transcurrido en días desde el evento de estacion astronómica anterior.

sun_rise_az.body_en:
Azimuth of the sunrise point on the horizon for the observer site on the calendar day of this season event.

Measured in degrees clockwise from true North: 90° is due East, values below 90° are north of East, and values above 90° are south of East.
sun_rise_az.body_es:
Azimut del punto de salida del Sol en el horizonte para el sitio del observador en el día de calendario de este evento estacional.

Se mide en grados en sentido horario desde el norte verdadero: 90° es el Este exacto, valores menores de 90° quedan al norte del Este y valores mayores de 90° al sur del Este.

sun_set_az.body_en:
Azimuth of the sunset point on the horizon for the observer site on the calendar day of this season event.

Measured in degrees clockwise from true North: 270° is due West, values below 270° are north of West, and values above 270° are south of West.
sun_set_az.body_es:
Azimut del punto de puesta del Sol en el horizonte para el sitio del observador en el día de calendario de este evento estacional.

Se mide en grados en sentido horario desde el norte verdadero: 270° es el Oeste exacto, valores menores de 270° quedan al norte del Oeste y valores mayores de 270° al sur del Oeste.

sun_rise_time.body_en:
Local solar time of sunrise for the observer site on the calendar day of this season event.

The value is computed from the shared observer location and shown as local solar clock time.
sun_rise_time.body_es:
Hora solar local de la salida del Sol para el sitio del observador en el día de calendario de este evento estacional.

El valor se calcula a partir de la ubicación compartida del observador y se muestra como hora de reloj solar local.

sun_set_time.body_en:
Local solar time of sunset for the observer site on the calendar day of this season event.

The value is computed from the shared observer location and shown as local solar clock time.
sun_set_time.body_es:
Hora solar local de la puesta del Sol para el sitio del observador en el día de calendario de este evento estacional.

El valor se calcula a partir de la ubicación compartida del observador y se muestra como hora de reloj solar local.

first_quarter.body_en: First Quarter (first): the Moon has completed one quarter of its orbit since the last new moon. The eastern half of the disc is illuminated — a half-moon visible in the afternoon and evening sky.
first_quarter.body_es: Cuarto creciente (first): la Luna ha completado un cuarto de su órbita desde la ultima luna nueva.

full_moon.body_en: Full Moon (full): the Moon is opposite the Sun in the sky; the entire near-side disc is illuminated. Rises at sunset, sets at sunrise.
full_moon.body_es: Luna llena (full): la Luna esta opuesta al Sol en el cielo; todo el disco cercaño aparece iluminado.

last_quarter.body_en: Last Quarter (last): the Moon has completed three quarters of its orbit since the last new moon. The western half of the disc is illuminated — a half-moon visible in the late night and morning sky.
last_quarter.body_es: Cuarto menguante (last): la Luna ha completado tres cuartos de su órbita desde la ultima luna nueva.

new_moon.body_en:
New Moon (new): the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the illuminated hemisphere faces away from us. The Moon is invisible or barely visible as a thin crescent at dusk/dawn.

One synodic month ≈ 29.5 days from new moon to new moon.
new_moon.body_es: Luna nueva (new): la Luna esta entre la Tierra y el Sol; el hemisferio iluminado mira en sentido opuesto a nosotros.

northern_solstice.body_en:
The northern (summer) solstice: the instant when the Sun reaches its maximum declination north of the celestial equator.

  • Northern Hemisphere: beginning of astronomical summer (verano) — longest day of the year
  • Southern Hemisphere: beginning of astronomical winter (invierno) — shortest day of the year
northern_solstice.body_es: Solsticio norte (de verano): instante en que el Sol alcanza su declinación maxima al norte del ecuador celeste.

northward_equinox.body_en:
The northward (vernal) equinox: the instant when the Sun crosses the celestial equator moving northward. Day and night are nearly equal in length.

  • Northern Hemisphere: beginning of astronomical spring (primavera)
  • Southern Hemisphere: beginning of astronomical autumn (otoño)

Computed with Sun.next_seasons() via PyEphem.
northward_equinox.body_es: Equinoccio rumbo al norte (vernal): instante en que el Sol cruza el ecuador celeste moviendose hacia el norte.

southern_solstice.body_en:
The southern (winter) solstice: the instant when the Sun reaches its maximum declination south of the celestial equator.

  • Northern Hemisphere: beginning of astronomical winter (invierno) — shortest day of the year
  • Southern Hemisphere: beginning of astronomical summer (verano) — longest day of the year
southern_solstice.body_es: Solsticio sur (de invierno): instante en que el Sol alcanza su declinación maxima al sur del ecuador celeste.

southward_equinox.body_en:
The southward (autumnal) equinox: the instant when the Sun crosses the celestial equator moving southward. Day and night are nearly equal in length.

  • Northern Hemisphere: beginning of astronomical autumn (otoño)
  • Southern Hemisphere: beginning of astronomical spring (primavera)
southward_equinox.body_es: Equinoccio rumbo al sur (otonal): instante en que el Sol cruza el ecuador celeste moviendose hacia el sur.

map.body_en:
Celestial map in a fixed Mercator-style projection. Use the Northern Hemisphere and Southern Hemisphere tabs to switch views.

Window size — give the map panel enough space by enlarging the application window or dragging the splitter between the controls and the map. The map is drawn at a fixed aspect ratio; if the panel is too narrow or too short, edges may be clipped.

No scroll bars — when the map does not fit, clipped regions are not reachable; resize the window or splitter instead of expecting pan or scroll.

No zoom — this projection does not support zoom or pan. Use Limiting magnitude and the display options on the left to change what is shown, and hover over stars and bodies for coordinates.
map.body_es:
Mapa celeste en proyeccion fija estilo Mercator. Usa las pestanas Hemisferio norte y Hemisferio sur para cambiar de vista.

Si el panel es pequeno, amplia la ventana o mueve el divisor entre controles y mapa.

bodies_on_map.body_en:
Select solar-system bodies to plot as emoji symbols on the map: Sun, Moon, and the classical planets.

Positions use the observer site and local time. Bodies below the horizon can be shown when the Horizon line is enabled (stars below the horizon are tinted green).
bodies_on_map.body_es: Selecciona cuerpos del sistema solar para graficar como símbolos: Sol, Luna y planetas clásicos.

configuration.body_en: Meridian view — rotate the map so the local meridian (LST) is at the top. Angular grid labels show absolute RA meridians; otherwise RA increases clockwise from 0° at the top.
configuration.body_es: Vista meridiana: rota el mapa para que el meridiano local (LST) quede arriba.

constellation_set.body_en:
Choose which asterism catalogue draws the stick figures and labels on the map. Stick figures and names are loaded from constellationship_*.fab and constellation_names_*.fab in montu/data.

  • IAU Constellations — the modern 88-constellation outlines used in contemporary astronomy.
  • Ancient Egyptian — late and earlier Egyptian sky figures (decans and related lore). Names and line patterns follow Egyptian tradition rather than the Greco-Roman zodiac; for example, Cancer appears as the Scarab Beetle and a Lion figure near the Scales corresponds to Centaurus, not Leo. Planets were the “stars that knew no rest,” each with Egyptian epithets (e.g. Júpiter as Horus Who Limits the Two Lands).
  • Dendera Egyptian — figures mapped onto the stars from the sculpted zodiac on the ceiling of the Hathor temple at Dendera (Ptolemaic/Roman period; commonly dated c. 54 BCE). It is not a purely Egyptian sky: the zodiac and many surrounding figures blend Greco-Roman, Babylonian, and Egyptian iconography drawn in Egyptian style — e.g. Gemini as Shu & Tefnut, Aquarius as the Nile god Hapi, and native Egyptian forms such as the Bull’s Thigh (Ursa Major) beside Babylonian Fox and Ewe.

Source — the Egyptian sets reproduce Stellarium sky-culture data (historical, Northern Africa). Ancient Egyptian is based on Juan Antonio Belmonte’s A Map of the Ancient Egyptian Firmament (contributed by Karrie Berglund; planet names updated by misibacsi). Dendera Egyptian maps figures from Louvre photographs of the Dendera ceiling (Susanne M. Hoffmann).

Licence — Ancient Egyptian: GNU GPL v2.0 (commercial and non-commercial use; adaptation and sharing allowed). Dendera Egyptian: CC BY-ND 4.0 (reuse with attribution; adapted versions may not be redistributed). See Stellarium for full sky-culture terms.
constellation_set.body_es:
Elige que catálogo de asterismos dibuja figuras y nombres en el mapa. Se cargan desde archivos constellationship_*.fab y constellation_names_*.fab.

  • Constelaciones UAI: 88 constelaciones modernas.
  • Egipcio antiguo: figuras celestes egipcias tardías y tempranas.
  • Egipcio de Dendera: figuras mapeadas desde el zodiaco de Dendera.

lines_on_map.body_en:
Overlay great circles on the map:

  • Ecliptic — apparent path of the Sun, precessed to the selected date (dashed orange).
  • Horizon — elevation 0° at the observer; enables azimuth labels and green below-horizon styling (solid green).
lines_on_map.body_es:
Superpone círculos mayores:

  • Eclíptica: trayectoria aparente del Sol.
  • Horizonte: elevación 0° en el sitio del observador.

predefined_site.body_en: Optional predefined ancient-world site. When selected, latitude, longitude, and altitude are filled automatically. Choose optional to search the global NASA catalogue without a specific observer.
predefined_site.body_es: Sitio predefinido opcional del mundo antiguo. Al seleccionarlo se rellenan latitud, longitud y altitud. Elige opcional para buscar en el catálogo global NASA sin observador específico.

latitude.body_en: Observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive. Together with longitude, it defines the site used to compute local eclipse circumstances and to filter results to eclipses visible above the horizon.
latitude.body_es: Latitud del observador en grados decimales, positiva al norte. Junto con la longitud define el sitio para calcular circunstancias locales y filtrar eclipses visibles.

longitude.body_en: Observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive. Both latitude and longitude are required for local visibility filtering and for the local columns in the results table.
longitude.body_es: Longitud del observador en grados decimales, positiva al este. Latitud y longitud son necesarias para el filtrado por visibilidad local.

altitude.body_en: Observer altitude above sea level in metres. Optional.
altitude.body_es: Altitud del observador sobre el nivel del mar en metros. Opcional.

year_start.body_en: Start of the search interval. Use BCE/CE and a positive historical year (e.g. 1700 BCE).
year_start.body_es: Inicio del intervalo de búsqueda. Usa AEC/EC y un año histórico positivo (p. ej. 1700 AEC).

year_end.body_en: End of the search interval. Years are converted internally to the NASA catalogue numbering.
year_end.body_es: Fin del intervalo de búsqueda. Los años se convierten internamente a la numeración del catálogo NASA.

date.body_en:
Filter eclipses in the NASA Five Millennium catalogue by calendar date.

Eclipse years and the dates shown in the results table use MontuPython's Mixed Julian/Gregorian proleptic calendar (Time.readable.datemix): Julian rules before 15 October 1582, Gregorian rules from the historical reform onward, extended consistently for ancient dates. Years are entered and displayed as positive historical BCE or CE counts (e.g. 596 BCE, 2024 CE).

Use From year and To year for the search interval; Month and Day optionally narrow it further.
date.body_es:
Filtra eclipses del catálogo NASA de cinco milenios por fecha de calendario.

Los años y las fechas mostradas en los resultados usan el calendario juliano/gregoriano mixto proléptico de MontuPython (Time.readable.datemix): reglas julianas antes del 15 de octubre de 1582 y gregorianas desde la reforma, extendidas de forma uniforme a fechas antiguas. Los años se ingresan y muestran como recuentos históricos positivos AEC o EC (p. ej. 596 AEC, 2024 EC).

Usa Desde año y Hasta año para el intervalo de búsqueda; Mes y Día lo restringen opcionalmente.

month.body_en: Optional month filter. Choose (any) to include all months in the year range.
month.body_es: Filtro opcional de mes. Elige (cualquiera) para incluir todos los meses del rango.

day.body_en: Optional day filter, enabled when a month is selected. Use (any) to include all days of that month.
day.body_es: Filtro opcional de día, activo cuando hay un mes seleccionado. Usa (cualquiera) para incluir todos los días de ese mes.

eclipse_types.body_en:
Select which eclipse classes to include from the NASA Five Millennium catalogue. At least one type must remain checked.

  • Total — the Moon fully covers the solar disk along the central path (umbra).
  • Annular — the Moon is too small to cover the Sun completely; a bright ring remains at greatest eclipse.
  • Hybrid — along the path the eclipse appears total at some locations and annular at others (short central durations).
  • Partial — only part of the Sun is obscured; the observer lies outside the central total/annular track.

These filters apply to the catalogue classification at greatest eclipse, before any local visibility filter.
eclipse_types.body_es:
Elige qué clases de eclipse incluir del catálogo NASA de cinco milenios. Debe permanecer al menos un tipo marcado.

  • Total — la Luna cubre por completo el disco solar a lo largo de la trayectoria central (umbra).
  • Anular — la Luna es demasiado pequeña para cubrir el Sol por completo; queda un anillo brillante en el máximo.
  • Híbrido — a lo largo de la trayectoria el eclipse es total en algunos lugares y anular en otros (duraciones centrales cortas).
  • Parcial — solo parte del Sol queda oculta; el observador está fuera de la franja central total/anular.

Estos filtros se aplican a la clasificación del catálogo en el eclipse máximo, antes de cualquier filtro de visibilidad local.

duration_min.body_en: Minimum central-line duration in seconds. Applies to total, annular, and hybrid eclipses with a defined duration_secs in the catalogue. Leave empty for no lower limit.
duration_min.body_es: Duración mínima de la línea central en segundos. Aplica a eclipses totales, anulares e híbridos con duration_secs definido. Deja vacío para sin límite inferior.

duration_max.body_en: Maximum central-line duration in seconds. Leave empty for no upper limit.
duration_max.body_es: Duración máxima de la línea central en segundos. Deja vacío para sin límite superior.

saros.body_en: Optional Saros number from the NASA catalogue (e.g. 139 for the 2017 and 2024 total-eclipse series). Leave empty to include all Saros cycles in the date range.
saros.body_es: Número de Saros opcional del catálogo NASA (p. ej. 139 para la serie de eclipses totales de 2017 y 2024). Deja vacío para incluir todos los ciclos Saros en el rango de fechas.

magnitude.body_en: Filter by eclipse magnitude at maximum for the selected observer, expressed as a percentage of the Sun's apparent diameter covered by the Moon. Values below 100% indicate a partial eclipse at the site; 100% or more can occur for total, annular, or deep partial eclipses depending on type. Leave min or max empty for no limit.
magnitude.body_es: Filtra por la magnitud del eclipse en el máximo para el observador seleccionado, expresada como porcentaje del diámetro aparente del Sol cubierto por la Luna. Valores por debajo del 100% indican un eclipse parcial en el sitio; 100% o más pueden darse en eclipses totales, anulares o parciales profundos según el tipo. Deja min o max vacío para sin límite.

elevation.body_en: Filter by the Sun's altitude at maximum eclipse for the observer, in degrees above the astronomical horizon. Useful to exclude eclipses that occur too low in the sky. Leave min or max empty for no limit.
elevation.body_es: Filtra por la altitud del Sol en el máximo del eclipse para el observador, en grados sobre el horizonte astronómico. Útil para excluir eclipses demasiado bajos en el cielo. Deja min o max vacío para sin límite.

azimuth.body_en: Filter by the Sun's azimuth at maximum eclipse for the observer, measured clockwise from north (0° = north, 90° = east). Leave min or max empty for no limit.
azimuth.body_es: Filtra por el azimut del Sol en el máximo del eclipse para el observador, medido en sentido horario desde el norte (0° = norte, 90° = este). Deja min o max vacío para sin límite.

local_duration.body_en: Filter by the total duration of the eclipse as seen from the observer, in seconds from first to last contact (C1 to C4). This is the local eclipse duration, not the central-line duration in the catalogue. Leave min or max empty for no limit.
local_duration.body_es: Filtra por la duración total del eclipse vista desde el observador, en segundos desde el primer al último contacto (C1 a C4). Es la duración local, no la de la línea central del catálogo. Deja min o max vacío para sin límite.

eclipse.body_en: MontuPython identifier for the catalogue entry: em_nasa_ followed by the NASA catalogue number (cat_no).
eclipse.body_es: Identificador MontuPython de la entrada del catálogo: em_nasa_ seguido del número de catálogo NASA (cat_no).

date.body_en: Calendar date of the eclipse in historical BCE/CE notation (year, month, day). Dates follow the NASA Five Millennium catalogue numbering.
date.body_es: Fecha de calendario del eclipse en notación histórica AEC/EC (año, mes, día). Las fechas siguen la numeración del catálogo NASA de cinco milenios.

type.body_en: Eclipse classification at greatest eclipse: Total, Annular, Hybrid, or Partial, derived from the NASA catalogue type code.
type.body_es: Clasificación del eclipse en el máximo: Total, Anular, Híbrido o Parcial, según el código de tipo del catálogo NASA.

saros.body_en: Saros cycle number assigned in the NASA catalogue. Eclipses separated by one Saros (~18 years 11 days) share similar geometry.
saros.body_es: Número de ciclo Saros asignado en el catálogo NASA. Eclipses separados por un Saros (~18 años 11 días) comparten geometría similar.

greatest_location.body_en: Geographic coordinates where the eclipse reaches its maximum on Earth's surface (latitude and longitude of greatest eclipse). The ( map ) link opens Xavier Jubier's interactive path map for the eclipse.
greatest_location.body_es: Coordenadas geográficas donde el eclipse alcanza su máximo en la superficie terrestre (latitud y longitud del eclipse máximo). El enlace ( mapa ) abre el mapa interactivo de la trayectoria de Xavier Jubier.

duration.body_en: Duration of totality or annularity at greatest eclipse along the central line, from the NASA catalogue (duration_secs). Shown as HH:MM:SS. Hybrid and partial eclipses may show a very short or zero central duration.
duration.body_es: Duración de la totalidad o anularidad en el eclipse máximo a lo largo de la línea central, del catálogo NASA (duration_secs). Se muestra como HH:MM:SS. Eclipses híbridos y parciales pueden mostrar una duración central muy corta o cero.

local_duration.body_en: Total duration of the eclipse as seen from your observer site, from first contact (C1) to last contact (C4), computed by MontuPython from the Besselian elements.
local_duration.body_es: Duración total del eclipse vista desde tu sitio de observación, desde el primer contacto (C1) hasta el último (C4), calculada por MontuPython a partir de los elementos besselianos.

maximum_local_time.body_en: Local solar time at the observer when the eclipse reaches maximum obscuration (instant of greatest magnitude at the site).
maximum_local_time.body_es: Hora solar local en el observador cuando el eclipse alcanza la máxima oscuración (instante de mayor magnitud en el sitio).

magnitude.body_en: Eclipse magnitude at maximum for the observer: percentage of the Sun's apparent diameter covered by the Moon. Computed from the catalogue Besselian elements for your site.
magnitude.body_es: Magnitud del eclipse en el máximo para el observador: porcentaje del diámetro aparente del Sol cubierto por la Luna. Calculada a partir de los elementos besselianos del catálogo para tu sitio.

sun_altitude.body_en: Sun's altitude above the astronomical horizon at maximum eclipse for the observer, in degrees.
sun_altitude.body_es: Altitud del Sol sobre el horizonte astronómico en el máximo del eclipse para el observador, en grados.

contacts.body_en: Data opens a table of local contact times and Sun position at each contact. Map opens Xavier Jubier's local-circumstance map centred on your observer site.
contacts.body_es: Datos abre una tabla de tiempos de contacto locales y posición del Sol en cada contacto. Mapa abre el mapa de circunstancias locales de Xavier Jubier centrado en tu sitio de observación.

contact.body_en: Eclipse contact identifier: C1 (first contact), C2 (beginning of totality or annularity), Maximum, C3 (end of totality or annularity), C4 (last contact). Only contacts that occur above the horizon at your site are listed.
contact.body_es: Identificador de contacto del eclipse: C1 (primer contacto), C2 (inicio de totalidad o anularidad), Máximo, C3 (fin de totalidad o anularidad), C4 (último contacto). Solo se listan contactos que ocurren sobre el horizonte en tu sitio.

times_ut.body_en: Instant of the contact expressed as UTC time (HH:MM:SS). Computed from the Besselian elements and the ΔT value assumed for the eclipse.
times_ut.body_es: Instante del contacto expresado como hora UTC (HH:MM:SS). Calculado a partir de los elementos besselianos y el valor de ΔT adoptado para el eclipse.

local_solar_time.body_en: Local solar time at the observer for the contact, using MontuPython's longitude-based local time convention for the selected site.
local_solar_time.body_es: Hora solar local en el observador para el contacto, usando la convención de hora local basada en longitud de MontuPython para el sitio seleccionado.

sun_altitude.body_en: Sun's altitude above the astronomical horizon at the contact instant, in degrees, for the observer.
sun_altitude.body_es: Altitud del Sol sobre el horizonte astronómico en el instante del contacto, en grados, para el observador.

sun_azimuth.body_en: Sun's azimuth at the contact instant, measured clockwise from north (0° = north, 90° = east), in degrees.
sun_azimuth.body_es: Azimut del Sol en el instante del contacto, medido en sentido horario desde el norte (0° = norte, 90° = este), en grados.
